violations.text: The Person in charge did not assure compliance with critical code requirements. New Violation. Correct By: 11/17/2026

Raw shelled unpasteurized eggs were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods such as celery and guac (in BLC area) and butter packets and cream cheese in the bakery walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Items were replaced during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/17/2026

The quaternary ammonium concentration in the sanitizing solution of the power soak 3-bay sink was 0 parts per million (ppm). According to the manufacturer's use directions, the concentration of the quaternary ammonium must be 200 ppm. PIC manually mixed chemical during time of inspection. Dispenser to be properly adjusted; Service call was placed during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/17/2026

Food contact surfaces of the covered slicer in the hot kitchen area were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Slicer was cleaned and sanitized during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/17/2026

Rotisserie chicken was observed held between 117-120 degrees Fahrenheit at hot holding grab and go case, foods were assessed and reheated during time of inspection. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be maintained at 135 degrees Fahrenheit or above except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/17/2026

Sliced tomatoes, composed stuffing, feta cheese, and bag of lettuce and recently prepped ingredients in deli prep unit were observed held at 44-49 degrees Fahrenheit. Foods were assessed and time/temperature abused foods were voluntarily disposed of. Foods that were recently prepared were placed into other refrigeration to chill. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Service call was placed during time of inspection; Prep unit not to be used to hold TCS foods until prep unit can maintain an internal food temperature of 41 degrees Fahrenheit or less. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/17/2026

Establishment is not maintaining records for using Time as a Public Health Control for pizza slices. Permission to use Time as a Public Health Control is contingent upon maintenance of records and active managerial control. Pizza must not be held for more than 4 hours. Anything left must be discarded. The food must be marked or identified to indicate the time that it must be used by or discarded. A log must be kept. Please retain records for at least 90 days and make records available to inspectors upon request. TPHC process, logs, and approval letter provided to PIC during time of inspection. Pizza that was observed at 124 degrees Fahrenheit was reheated during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/17/2026

Quaternary ammonium sanitizer solution in the meatcutting room, produce room and bakery were in excess of 500 parts per million (ppm). A quaternary ammonia sanitizer solution applied to food contact surfaces must be applied at the strength as indicated on the manufacturers' label. Corrective action is to manually mix chemical and check concentration of solution with test strips. Service call was placed for dispenser during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/17/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Stuffing for seafood was observed at 107 degrees Fahrenheit in 12 qt plastic cambro. Foods were assessed and placed into shallower food containers to continue with cooling process. Proper cooling methods reviewed during time of inspection. https://datahealth.ri.gov/publications/factsheets/CoolFoodsRapidly.pdf New Violation. Correct By: 11/17/2026

The cutting board block on prep unit in hot food serving area and back BLC prep area very scratched and scored. Cutting blocks and boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced. New Violation. Correct By: 12/17/2026
Refrigerator door gaskets for 2 door reach-in in BLC kitchen and 1 door-reach in in deli front counter area were observed in poor repair. PIC informed. New Violation. Correct By: 12/17/2026
The following were observed in poor repair:-bakery walk-in cooler floors-produce prep room floorsThe physical facilities must be maintained in good repair. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 08/21/2026

Floor tile near seafood area handwashing sink and under and around seafood display case were observed in poor repair. The physical facilities must be maintained in good repair. Approved Finish Schedule provided during time of inspection. https://datahealth.ri.gov/publications/requirements/FoodProtectionAppovedFinishSchedule.pdf New Violation. Correct By: 02/17/2027

Per interview of PIC, meat, chourice and spinach pies from an unapproved source are sold in establishment. No product was available during time of visit. Approved Food Source guidance document provided during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/29/2026

The hand-washing sink in the hot foods service area was blocked by hotel pans and utensils were observed in hand sink. A hand-washing sink shall be accessible at all times for employee use. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/21/2025

-Molluscan Shellfish (clams) located in (seafood display case) did not have the proper identification tags. Molluscan Shellstock tags must remain attached to the container in which the Molluscan Shellstock are received until the container is empty. Tag was located and placed with Shellstock during time of inspection. -Molluscan shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. PIC informed. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/21/2025

Raw animal foods (such as chicken and beef) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (such as cut vegetables) in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/21/2025

Quaternary ammonium sanitizer solution was in excess of 500 parts per million (ppm). A quaternary ammonia sanitizer solution applied to food contact surfaces must be applied at the strength as indicated on the manufacturers' label. Establishment must manually adjust sanitizer concentration until unit is properly adjusted. New Violation. Correct By: 08/28/2025
The following were observed in poor repair: -gaskets for coolers throughout the facility -top lid for pizza prep unit New Violation. Correct By: 10/21/2025

The cutting boards in the hot foods service area and produce prep room are very scratched and scored. Cutting blocks and boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced. New Violation. Correct By: 09/21/2025

The non-food contact surfaces of the following have an accumulation of residue and debris: -shrimp chest freezer (ice accumulation) -large walk-in freezer (ice accumulation) -ice machine in BLC area New Violation. Correct By: 09/04/2025
Hot water was not available at hand washing sink in BLC area during time of inspection. Per PIC, work order is in place. New Violation. Correct By: 08/28/2025
3 bay sink in bakery area observed leaking. Equipment and system to be in good repair and proper adjustment. New Violation. Correct By: 09/04/2025
The following were observed in poor repair: -bakery walk-in cooler floors -produce prep room floors The physical facilities must be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 08/21/2026

Various grab and go prepared meals were observed held at (44-47) degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Grab and go prepared meals that were placed on retail shelves yesterday were voluntarily disposed of. Meals that were placed today were placed into refrigeration to chill. Corrected On-Site. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 06/05/2024

Shelf 5 of open air case used for grab and go foods was observed at ranging ambient temperatures of 44-46 degrees Fahrenheit. Shelf was taken out of service to hold potentially hazardous foods. Equipment to be proper adjusted/ replaced/ repaired. Unit can only hold potentially hazardous foods if internal temperature of food is maintained at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below. New Violation. Correct By: 06/12/2024

The ceiling in the food preparation areas is covered with tiles that are not smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. Materials for surfaces shall be smooth, durable, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent for areas subject to moisture such as food preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, ware-washing areas, and toilet rooms. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 02/15/2024

Cheese and various grab and go prepared meals were observed held at (44-54) degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Foods were observed to be stored above open air case's load limit. Cheeses were placed into other refrigeration during time of inspection. Grab n go prepared meals that were placed into open air cases for retail sale yesterday were voluntarily disposed of. See disposal. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/22/2024

Thermometers are lacking in the preparation refrigeration unit(s). Cold holding equipment used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods must have at least one thermometer that is located to allow easy viewing of the temperature display. New Violation. Correct By: 06/05/2024

Wood is used in the construction of the lined shelves of prep tables in the deli and meat/seafood area. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other food soiling or that require frequent cleaning must be constructed of a nonabsorbent and smooth material. New Violation. Correct By: 06/22/2024

The cutting board in the meat room is very scratched and scored. Cutting blocks and boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced. New Violation. Correct By: 06/05/2024
3 bay sink in deli area was observed leaking at faucet in deli area. 3 bay sink in seafood area leaking from drainage pipes. Equipment to be properly adjusted. New Violation. Correct By: 06/05/2024

Area surrounding oil disposal units were observed with an accumulation of leaf litter and grease. Area to be maintained cleaned to prevent any harborage conditions for pests. New Violation. Correct By: 06/05/2024

The ceiling in the food preparation areas is covered with tiles that are not smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. Materials for surfaces shall be smooth, durable, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent for areas subject to moisture such as food preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, ware-washing areas, and toilet rooms. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 02/15/2024
Produce receiving door/gate is in poor repair. The physical facilities must be maintained in good repair. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 06/22/2024

The following has an accumulation of soil residue and food debris: 1. Large Walk-in freezer (ice accumulation) 2. Fanguards and fanguard hairnets in produce walk-in cooler and refrigerated meat room. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 06/05/2024
